lxc_b750e9cc97c428b5.text: Picture a red mushroom with white spots.

lxc_217a548670f5522f.text: It appears in fairy tales, children's books, video games and Christmas decorations.

lxc_4f14dc5a80beb630.text: It looks friendly, almost like a toy.

lxc_cec911e6b32263f6.text: But this mushroom, the fly agaric, is poisonous.

lxc_26bb41f5f6604db1.text: So why is a poisonous mushroom so popular in our culture?

lxc_d83cb5862c76f843.text: And did people in Europe really eat it in the past?

lxc_2d57107b58cf6430.text: You will learn where the fly agaric grows and how it got its name.

lxc_fe9a260a9e63e731.text: You will also find out which people are known for using it and why.

lxc_f6cf90fc56882ec6.text: Next, you will meet its two main chemicals and see how they affect the brain.

lxc_bf788f7125360127.text: Finally, you will compare it with "magic mushrooms" and decide whether they really belong together.

lxc_e8b264b214022c38.text: Along the way, you will practise an important skill: separating what is well recorded from what is only an exciting story.

lxc_e314a531ba8a4984.text: The fly agaric's scientific name is Amanita muscaria.

lxc_0a8ec84b808d45e7.text: It has a red cap with white spots and a white stalk.

lxc_f02e440734f813d8.text: In Britain and Ireland it is widespread, and it grows in woodland and at the edges of woods.

lxc_ebd02da5040d63f0.text: You often find it near birch, pine and spruce trees, and this is not an accident.

lxc_73621791fc782cfc.text: The mushroom we can see is only a small part of the fungus.

lxc_4fddfaf44a3805b8.text: It is the fruiting body, a bit like the fruit on a tree.

lxc_86e99dcbd7185c58.text: Under the ground there is a large network of thin threads called mycelium.

lxc_e937a107403f4d83.text: This network connects with tree roots, and the two work as partners.

lxc_123a7dd5aee23ede.text: The fungus gives the tree nutrients from the soil, and the tree gives the fungus sugars.

lxc_8d7043081227c771.text: So a fly agaric next to a birch tree is part of a team.

lxc_eb9dc7b609d6acd4.text: The white spots also have a story.

lxc_bd8514a9e7428b78.text: When the mushroom is young, a protective layer called a veil covers it.

lxc_bc08806636f023cb.text: As the cap grows, the veil breaks, and the white spots are pieces that stay behind.

lxc_c8f93600e58c54c7.text: Rain can wash them away, so some fly agarics have no spots at all.

lxc_254729f9bb05a259.text: This is one reason why colour and spots are not a reliable way to judge a mushroom.

lxc_90f5d8747102f414.text: The English name comes from history.

lxc_e5edd1bef1fd4a24.text: In the past, people used the mushroom against flies and other insects.

lxc_f59706d95126c87b.text: It was a kind of insecticide, a substance that kills insects.

lxc_51cb57654295ca8e.text: Notice what the name tells us and what it does not tell us.

lxc_0992ad1a2abdcb1d.text: It shows that people found a practical use for the mushroom.

lxc_64d902a305327314.text: However, it does not show that they ate it.

lxc_1b8f106aa59d2544.text: In fact, eating it can cause hallucinations and painful stomach cramps.

lxc_6697eeb786380aa6.text: However, its fame in European culture does not show that Europeans traditionally ate it.

lxc_e75bf8ce4ee6e68f.text: In northern Eurasia, especially Siberia, several groups used the fly agaric.

lxc_1cd6bfafa2792e65.text: These included the Nenets, Yukaghir, Koryak and Chukchi peoples.

lxc_7a7f285ef5bfb94e.text: Sometimes they used it for fun and relaxation, and sometimes they used it in rituals.

lxc_701f37189082224e.text: The mushroom could create dream-like experiences.

lxc_c24ea7d5e7328267.text: Some people believed that, during these experiences, they met their ancestors or spirits.

lxc_92eb36a6eec24c68.text: This was their belief and part of their way of understanding the world.

lxc_a358d4095d7c40ae.text: It is not a scientific fact about the mushroom.

lxc_48b869719e80b5cf.text: Here the picture is much less clear.

lxc_d37e940bda7677f4.text: There is one story of Sámi people using the fly agaric in Finland.

lxc_77f6a77d58b8228e.text: However, it is a single personal report, and it may describe something rare or isolated.

lxc_42f33e3a65ea78bd.text: One story cannot prove that a whole tradition existed.

lxc_2a96770aa9d5071e.text: So we cannot say that the Sámi, or Europeans in general, regularly used the mushroom.

lxc_ef3a257ce35c672b.text: You may also hear exciting stories about Viking warriors eating fly agaric before battle.

lxc_171659355ca1ced3.text: Stories like these spread easily because they are dramatic.

lxc_044d868c2346dee8.text: But the well-recorded use comes from Siberia, not from Viking Europe.

lxc_76e13239b5f9f656.text: A good rule is this: if a story is very exciting but has no clear record behind it, treat it as a guess.

lxc_47a2e9a2ae15565e.text: Modern myths about this mushroom are common, and many of them are more sensational than true.

lxc_5815448fd17e75a8.text: Why does the fly agaric affect people at all?

lxc_f28ac841f1f9f977.text: The two main chemicals are ibotenic acid and muscimol.

lxc_075676dba89249b1.text: The main effects on the mind are linked to muscimol.

lxc_1866769949aed4c8.text: To understand muscimol, think about how the brain sends messages.

lxc_4183d555eb66f458.text: Brain cells talk to each other with chemical messages.

lxc_c49efb36af1ea58a.text: Each message needs a receptor, a receiving place on a cell, like a lock that accepts only certain keys.

lxc_176a20537189c2c2.text: One important messenger is called GABA.

lxc_e14ba0b70875420a.text: GABA usually tells brain cells to calm down and send fewer signals, a bit like a brake in a car.

lxc_98c4b826b512a023.text: Muscimol acts on GABA-A receptors, so it pushes on this braking system.

lxc_139763cb7c3d1a05.text: You might expect a brake to make a person simply sleepy.

lxc_6a4461190639c20d.text: However, the effects of the fly agaric are stranger than that.

lxc_2d3ce95ee34cddff.text: A person may feel very sleepy and then suddenly become restless and agitated.

lxc_6d704286784274c3.text: These states can change back and forth.

lxc_bfb61c29e20699b3.text: People can also become confused, see the world differently, have hallucinations or fall into delirium, a serious state of mental confusion.

lxc_fb1d1e2a961f8514.text: The amount of these chemicals is different from one mushroom to another.

lxc_11f968d8672a2c51.text: Because of this, a person’s reaction can be difficult to predict.

lxc_5036703ff72d3a87.text: This is a key reason why the fly agaric is treated as poisonous, not as a harmless natural experience.

lxc_4f6cb40d08e80f72.text: People often put the fly agaric in the same group as "magic mushrooms".

lxc_b9b84e1cac18ea24.text: Usually, "magic mushrooms" means mushrooms that contain psilocybin, mostly from a group called Psilocybe.

lxc_53332f321c50a6f2.text: So is the fly agaric one of them?

lxc_07262d24f53920fb.text: To answer, we need to compare how they work.

lxc_a53b5182cfa016f5.text: In the body, psilocybin changes into another chemical called psilocin.

lxc_3ebe1d8bf4d02f73.text: Psilocin acts on receptors for serotonin, another brain messenger, especially the type called 5-HT2A.

lxc_098b67c9c067f379.text: Muscimol, as you saw, works through the GABA system instead.

lxc_93aaffc350608f69.text: Serotonin and GABA are separate signalling systems.

lxc_8df29de0a9b1df5a.text: So the two mushrooms are like two different keys that open two different locks.

lxc_9128b91c1e9455e0.text: This leads to a clear answer.

lxc_0918058b867534df.text: In a broad sense, both mushrooms are psychoactive, which means they change how the mind works and how people see the world.

lxc_9898e5b318b4d633.text: Because of that shared effect, it makes cultural sense to talk about them together, for example in history or in stories.

lxc_9e5f3746c8974049.text: But it does not make scientific sense to treat them as the same thing.

lxc_7b5397b46ced5150.text: The fly agaric is not a psilocybin mushroom.

lxc_3d6d978ec77f6e74.text: Its chemicals are different, they act in a different way, and one cannot replace the other.

lxc_ea946ebd81160155.text: There is also a practical lesson.

lxc_39382bea817a897c.text: You cannot tell mushrooms apart safely just by looking at them.

lxc_6368aa767a16f2bd.text: Even experts use much more than appearance, so a picture or a colour is never enough.

lxc_0288fc7aa9fbe23c.text: Today, the fly agaric is not only a forest mushroom or a fairy-tale picture.

lxc_bebcb01b1a7632b3.text: It has also become a product.

lxc_3a4d4bcf457d98b2.text: In 2025, the German Federal Institute for Risk Assessment warned about gummies and other food-like products containing muscimol.

lxc_1df6df7445c361ff.text: Both teenagers and adults were using them for fun, and poison centres were receiving cases.

lxc_3ccc2a11ce456e89.text: Children are especially at risk, because a gummy looks like an ordinary sweet.

lxc_ac61c05d0018a25d.text: A similar problem appeared in the United States.

lxc_593da9a6c6b8f285.text: In 2024, an investigation there tested mushroom gummies.

lxc_7d819df88cc8e24c.text: Some products said they contained Amanita or a mix of mushrooms.

lxc_e4cb45dbb08f4da3.text: However, several of them also contained psilocybin and psilocin, which were not on the label.

lxc_c8d107492f701cbe.text: Some people who ate gummies labelled with Amanita needed to be checked in hospital.

lxc_f461a0e548d2c31c.text: Be careful about what this shows.

lxc_961d48291b14f8ea.text: It does not mean that the fly agaric naturally contains psilocybin.

lxc_7d60c51eee00cbe9.text: It means that some factory-made products did not contain what their labels said.

lxc_d1e682444c696f37.text: Marketing often uses the word "mushroom" in a loose way, and this can mix up two groups that science keeps separate.

lxc_c71cf0a453585376.text: As a result, a buyer may not know what they are really eating.

lxc_727e10125f1ff577.text: This was also one small study in the US, so it does not tell us how common these products are in Europe.

lxc_e894fdac8f7a6d2c.text: In the US, the food safety authority has also stated that fly agaric and its chemicals are not approved for use in normal food.

lxc_38f8d66a4b9b90f7.text: It reported serious risks of poisoning.

lxc_c8b991cb9492d6e4.text: This is a US rule, not European law, but the main message applies everywhere.

lxc_94272a536473506a.text: A product is not safe just because it is natural, traditional, sold online or packed in a colourful box.

lxc_c730e8a180b7e08d.text: None of these things proves that a product is safe or that it works as medicine.
